name: Rich Eagle Ford Mainline (REM)
researcher_notes: Not on the roster under any name. The nearest rows are the NET Mexico Gas Pipeline (P0224) and the Regency intrastate line, which are different pipes. The pipeline is operating, so it was built and is no longer only proposed. An Oil and Gas Journal article from February 2012 says the first 160 miles of 30-inch pipe entered service in October 2011. The Energy Information Administration project table (August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 701) lists Expansion I as Completed, 160 miles, 30 inch, 400 MMcf/d added capacity, October 2011, Texas only, intrastate. Row 740 lists Expansion II as Completed, 70 miles, 42 inch, 400 MMcf/d, 2012. The two sources do not fully agree on the later phases. The article says a 60 mile 42-inch first expansion was due in late 2012 and a 37 mile 30-inch second expansion in late 2013, for 257 miles in all and more than 1 bcf/d. This row stages only the first 160 mile phase, where both sources agree. The 70 mile 42-inch phase (row 740, 2012) should be a separate expansion row once its length is settled, and it passes the 25 km test on its own. The 400 MMcf/d figure is the added capacity for that phase, not the whole system. Start and end points were not found in a source that could be checked, so they are left blank apart from the state. The line serves Eagle Ford shale gas in South Texas and was not found in any FERC document because it is intrastate. A Texas Railroad Commission check was not done. No route was researched. Owner is the team spelling Energy Transfer LP, found by the entity lookup. The operator is Energy Transfer Partners LP in both sources. Confidence is high.
